top_stories.title: Coinbase launches tokenized stocks on Base
points: Coinbase launched tokenized stocks (blockchain tokens representing shares of real company stock) on Base for eligible non-US users.
Creates a composable equity primitive (an interoperable financial building block) for the EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) stack.

Potential builder use cases include emerging-market neobrokerages pairing local stablecoins with US equity access, AI-driven personalized index creation, corporate loyalty programs distributing fractional shares, yield-principal stripping, AI agent-managed allocations, and futarchy-style decision markets (prediction markets used for organizational decisions).

items.title: Standard Chartered launches spot crypto trading in the UAE
points: Standard Chartered, a major traditional bank, now offers spot crypto trading (buying/selling cryptocurrencies at current market prices) to UAE customers.
This marks a shift from custody and derivatives to direct spot trading services by mainstream banks.
UAE continues positioning itself as a crypto-friendly regulatory hub, attracting institutional participation and potentially boosting investor confidence in digital assets.

items.title: New Jersey escalates prediction markets fight to Supreme Court
points: New Jersey filed a 332-page petition asking the Supreme Court to review a Third Circuit ruling favoring Kalshi in a cease-and-desist dispute over sports event contracts.

Core dispute: New Jersey claims states control gambling law; Kalshi says it can't operate under 50 different state regulators; the CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission) claims exclusive federal jurisdiction.
Escalation follows Kalshi's recent loss in a related Nevada case at the Ninth Circuit, highlighting fragmented rulings across federal circuits.

items.title: Bitcoin trades like 'amplified gold' amid Treasury selloff
points: Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold hit a 6-year high during Treasury bond selloffs.
BTC gained 22.4% in a week before pulling back to $77,600.

items.title: Real-world assets (RWA) emerge as crypto's next liquidity channel
points: RWAs (blockchain-based representations of physical assets like Treasuries and equities) have tripled to roughly $30B in value over 18 months.
Trailing-12-month inflows are 0.9% of market cap, ahead of DAT (digital asset treasury) performance but behind ETFs at the same maturity stage.

Unlike prior channels (VC/ICO, stablecoins, ETFs), RWAs let capital already in the system rotate into BTC or altcoins with less friction; peak inflows are estimated 2-3 years out, potentially producing longer, less volatile cycles.

items.title: Stablecoins alone can't fix remittances
points: Global remittance fees average 6.36%, versus a UN 2030 target of 3%; stablecoins address only 1 of 6 steps in a typical transfer pipeline.

On-chain liquidity pools can rebalance across 50 markets in minutes rather than days, cutting correspondent banking friction, though apps still need a balance sheet to operate (e.g., Félix Pago raised $200M).

Competing stablecoins (Circle, Tether, Stripe Bridge, Sony, Klarna, Cloudflare, Fiserv) don't interoperate, prompting a16z Crypto to fund Better Money ($10M round) for cross-stablecoin conversion, recreating the intermediary layer blockchains aimed to remove.

sections.title: 1. Prediction Markets Face Supreme Court Battle Over State vs. Federal Control
points: New Jersey filed a 332-page petition asking the Supreme Court to review a Third Circuit ruling that favored Kalshi in a cease-and-desist dispute over sports event contracts.
The core dispute: New Jersey argues states retain authority over gambling law; Kalshi argues it cannot operate under 50 different regulators; the CFTC claims exclusive jurisdiction.
This escalates ongoing conflicts—Kalshi recently lost a related case in Nevada at the Ninth Circuit, signaling deepening regulatory fragmentation across circuits.

sections.title: 2. Real-World Assets Emerge as Next Structural Liquidity Channel
points: Onchain tokenized value has tripled to ~$30B in 18 months, with trailing-12-month inflows of 0.9% of market cap—tracking ahead of DAT performance but behind ETFs at the same maturity stage.

Unlike prior channels (VC/ICO, stablecoins, ETFs) that attracted asset-specific buyers, RWAs place capital inside the system where purchases of tokenized Treasuries or equities can rotate into BTC or altcoins with reduced friction.

Tokenized assets are now accepted as collateral across major venues and DeFi protocols; if historical timing holds, peak RWA inflows are 2–3 years out, likely producing longer, less volatile cycles driven by balance-sheet holders.

sections.title: 3. Tokenized Stocks Launch on Base; Builders Sought Across Consumer and DeFi Use Cases
points: Coinbase launched tokenized stocks on Base for eligible non-US users, creating a composable equity primitive (an interoperable financial building block) for the EVM stack.

Consumer targets include emerging-market neobrokerages pairing local stablecoins with US equity access, AI-driven personalized index creation, and corporate loyalty programs distributing fractional share ownership instead of points.

DeFi applications span yield-principal stripping (separating interest from principal to enable self-repaying loans), AI agent-managed equity allocations, and futarchy-style decision markets (prediction markets used to make organizational decisions) tied to public corporations.

sections.title: 4. Stablecoin Fragmentation Creates New Intermediary Layer in Remittances
points: Global remittance fees average 6.36% against a 3% UN 2030 target; stablecoins address only 1 of 6 pipeline steps in a typical transfer, leaving FX working capital, compliance, and payout rails as bottlenecks.

Tokenized liquidity does reduce correspondent banking friction: on-chain pools rebalance across 50 markets in minutes rather than days, but even zero-distribution apps like Félix Pago ($200M raise) require a balance sheet to operate.

Multiple competing stablecoins (Circle, Tether, Stripe Bridge, Sony, Klarna, Cloudflare, Fiserv) don't interoperate cleanly, forcing a16z Crypto to fund Better Money ($10M round) for cross-stablecoin conversion—replicating the intermediary function blockchains were designed to eliminate.
